IR.rationale: A rising 1-year yield relative to Fed Funds signals that markets are pricing tighter policy. Tighter policy raises funding costs and pressures the leveraged carry and arbitrage positions held across hedge-fund strategies.

B.rationale: High-yield and EM corporate yields rising together mark a broad credit sell-off. Such a sell-off hurts credit-sensitive event-driven, distressed and arbitrage books, and spread changes tend to persist.

V.rationale: Volatility driven by financial-crisis news signals funding and liquidity stress. That stress forces deleveraging and depresses returns on liquidity-providing strategies.

AP.rationale: Strong emerging-market equity returns indicate a risk-on, global-growth regime. Most hedge-fund strategies have positive beta to this regime, and their stale pricing carries the effect into subsequent months.

TF.rationale: Large payoffs on short-rate trend straddles indicate abrupt rate repricing. Rate shocks tend to disrupt relative-value and macro positioning.

ST.rationale: A quality rally combined with weak reversal profits describes a flight to quality in which liquidity provision is unrewarded. This is a state in which hedge-fund alpha tends to be poor.

FX.rationale: A broadly weaker dollar, including against the commodity and carry currency AUD, reflects easy global dollar funding and risk appetite. Both support hedge-fund returns.

COM.rationale: Rising copper prices proxy for global growth momentum, which is a supportive backdrop for directional and event-driven strategies.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with elevated measured financial stress describe a funding-constrained environment. In such an environment leveraged arbitrage returns suffer.

ENDG.rationale: Hedge-fund index returns are positively autocorrelated because of illiquid-asset return smoothing and slow-moving capital, so recent strength tends to continue.

IR.rationale: Rising short-term bill rates raise funding costs and can trigger unwinds of leveraged positions. This raises the chance of a tail loss.

B.rationale: Simultaneous widening in European high-yield and EM corporate yields signals a global credit shock. Such shocks are the classic trigger of correlated drawdowns in credit and arbitrage strategies.

V.rationale: High equity volatility that is specifically driven by financial-crisis news marks systemic stress. Under systemic stress, margin calls and redemptions produce left-tail outcomes.

AP.rationale: Weak US and emerging equity markets together indicate a global risk-off episode. Hedge-fund losses during such episodes tend to cluster and extend.

TF.rationale: Large moves in short-rate trends indicate disruptive monetary repricing. This raises the risk of losses for rate-sensitive relative-value books.

ST.rationale: A flight to quality with unrewarded liquidity provision is characteristic of deleveraging episodes. Those episodes precede crowded-trade drawdowns.

FX.rationale: A broad dollar rally, including against carry currencies, signals tightening global dollar liquidity and risk aversion. This raises tail-loss risk.

COM.rationale: Falling oil and copper prices together signal a global demand shock. Such a shock hits energy credit, EM exposure and event-driven positions.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions during weak real activity is the macro-financial state in which funding and redemption spirals, and hence large losses, are most likely.

ENDG.rationale: Because of return smoothing and drawdown persistence, weak recent index returns raise the probability of further large losses.

IR.rationale: A falling 1-year yield relative to Fed Funds signals expected easing. Expected easing relieves funding pressure and supports rebounds in levered strategies.

B.rationale: Falling EM corporate and US high-yield yields describe a credit rally. Credit rallies generate strong gains in distressed, event-driven and convertible strategies.

V.rationale: Elevated volatility without a financial-crisis component offers dispersion and trading opportunities without funding stress. This favours upside outcomes.

AP.rationale: Strong emerging-market equity returns reflect global risk appetite. Under strong risk appetite, beta-heavy hedge-fund strategies can deliver right-tail returns.

TF.rationale: Strong short-rate trends signal large rate repricing. Such repricing shifts the distribution of macro and fixed-income relative-value payoffs.

ST.rationale: Weak profitability-factor returns mark a junk rally, a high-risk-appetite environment that tends to produce large hedge-fund gains.

FX.rationale: A strong Australian dollar signals carry-friendly, pro-growth conditions associated with right-tail hedge-fund performance.

COM.rationale: Rising copper prices indicate accelerating global demand. Accelerating demand supports directional, EM and event-driven positions.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress leaves assets cheap and arbitrage spreads wide. The subsequent normalisation can produce outsized gains for distressed and arbitrage strategies.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent index returns tend to persist through smoothing and momentum, raising the chance of a large gain.
